h1: Recorded Lecture Hosting in India: Why the Lowest-Cost Answer Is Hosting Included in Your Plan (2026)
dek: Storage is almost free. What costs money is delivering your lectures every time a student presses play. This guide shows what hosting really costs, compares the DIY routes Indian teachers use, and explains why hosting included in your teaching plan is the simple answer.
cover_alt: Recorded lecture hosting in India: storage is cheap and delivery is the real cost; the AllCoaching studio includes storage and streaming in every plan
audience: Indian teachers, tutors and coaching institutes who record lectures and sell them online
intro: The lowest-cost way for an Indian teacher to host recorded lectures is to use hosting that is already included in the platform you sell from, with storage and streaming priced into the plan. Buying cheap storage separately looks cheaper on day one, but the bill that grows is delivery, not storage.

Most teachers searching for "cheap video hosting" compare storage prices. Storage is the small cost. The cost that grows is bandwidth: every time a student streams a lecture, the data travels to their phone, and most hosting providers bill for that by the gigabyte. A library of fifty lectures can cost almost nothing to store and still produce a large bill in the month a batch actually watches it.
This guide explains the three parts of a hosting bill, compares the routes Indian teachers use, lists what good lecture hosting needs, and shows what AllCoaching includes in each plan.
takeaways: Delivery is the real cost: storage is cheap and paid once; bandwidth is billed per GB and grows with every view.
YouTube unlisted is not for paid lectures: anyone with the link can watch and share it.
Metered hosting gets dearer as you succeed: AWS, Bunny or Cloudflare Stream and your own server all bill more as students watch more, and you still build the player and logins.
Hosting included in a plan keeps cost known: storage and streaming come with the plan, with no per-view bill.

Hosting is solved; being found is not: spend the time you save on getting students to your lectures.

sections.h2: What is the lowest-cost way to host recorded lectures in India?
sections.html:
The lowest-cost way is hosting that comes inside the platform you teach and sell on, with storage and streaming included in the plan and no per-view bill. A separate storage plan looks cheaper until students start watching, because delivery is billed on top.

Ask a different question than "where is storage lowest-cost". Ask: what will hosting cost when my lectures are actually watched, and who pays for that? On a metered service, you pay more every month your course does well. On a plan with hosting included, the cost stays where you can see it.

When teachers ask us where to host their lectures cheaply, the first thing we point out is that they are about to pay separately for a problem the platform already solves, while the harder problem, getting students to watch, stays open.

sections.h2: What does recorded lecture hosting actually cost?
sections.html:
A hosting bill has three parts: storage, encoding and delivery. Storage and encoding are small; delivery (bandwidth) is the large, recurring part.

{{fig:cost-components|Video hosting cost components: storage is small, encoding happens once per upload, and delivery bandwidth is the large cost that grows with every view|Where a video hosting bill comes from. Bar lengths are illustrative.}}
CostWhat it isHow it growsSize
StorageKeeping the video filesWith library sizeSmall
EncodingMaking every quality for every deviceOnce per uploadModest
Delivery (bandwidth)Streaming to studentsWith every viewLarge

Public price lists show the gap. Bunny.net, a popular video and CDN provider, lists storage from $0.01 per GB a month per region, while delivery is billed per GB on top: from $0.005 per GB on its volume network, and $0.03 per GB for Asia on its standard network.[1] A lecture is stored once but delivered every time a student watches it, so a popular course can cost far more to deliver than to store.

Real hosting also needs encoding into several qualities and a content delivery network (CDN) so playback starts fast across India.[3] Raw storage includes neither. The technical side is covered in secure video hosting for educational content.

sections.h2: Why does DIY hosting cost more than the price you see?
sections.html:
Because a storage price leaves out the parts that grow: bandwidth, a player, access control and your own time.

{{fig:hidden-costs|Hidden costs of DIY video hosting: bandwidth that grows with views, encoding and a player, student logins and access control, and keys, updates and broken embeds|What a storage price leaves out.}}
  • Bandwidth that grows with views: the more your lectures are watched, the bigger the monthly bill.
  • Encoding and a player: you convert videos into several qualities and embed a working player, or pay for one.
  • Access control and student accounts: to keep paid lectures paid, you need logins and gating.
  • Maintenance: API keys, updates and broken embeds take hours you could spend teaching.

sections.h2: What does good lecture hosting need?
sections.html:
Good lecture hosting is storage plus fast delivery, adaptive playback, a player, phone-first viewing and access control, at a cost you know in advance.

{{fig:checklist|Checklist for recorded lecture hosting: fast delivery across India, smooth playback on weak networks, a reliable player, phone-first playback, access control and a known monthly cost|What good lecture hosting needs.}}
NeedWhy it mattersRaw storageHosting in a teaching platform
CDN deliveryFast start across IndiaNoYes
Adaptive streamingLess buffering on weak networksNoYes
Video playerPlays inside your website and appNoYes
Access controlOnly paying students watchNoYes
Known costNo surprise bill as you growNoYes

Adaptive streaming switches video quality to match each student's connection, so a lecture keeps playing on a weak mobile signal instead of stopping.[4] Most of your students will watch on phones, so this matters more than storage price. If you are moving from a YouTube channel to paid courses, read monetising a YouTube teaching channel with your own app.

sections.h2: Hosting is a commodity. Discovery is the lever.
sections.html:
Once hosting is included in your plan, the cost that decides your income is not storage but how many students find your lectures. A well-hosted course nobody finds earns nothing.

Put the time you would spend comparing storage plans into being found: a free demo lecture on YouTube, a course page that ranks for your exam, and a clear price. Your courses can also be discovered on the AllCoaching app by students searching your exam or subject, as explained in how the AllCoaching marketplace helps discovery.

Teachers keep shopping for cheaper shelves for videos nobody is watching yet. Storage was never the bill that mattered. Get hosting included in your plan and spend the time you save on being found.

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching

faq: What is the lowest-cost way to host recorded lectures in India?

The lowest-cost way is hosting included in the platform you teach and sell on, with storage and streaming priced into the plan and no per-view bill. On AllCoaching, Starter (₹6,999 a year, 10% per sale) includes 512 GB of storage and 100 GB of streaming a month, Growth (₹7,999 a month, 0% commission) 1 TB and 1 TB, and Pro (₹14,999 a month, 0% commission) 2 TB and 2 TB.
Is video hosting expensive because of storage or bandwidth?
Bandwidth. Storage is cheap and paid once, but delivery is billed per GB every time a student watches, so a small library watched by many students can cost more than a large library watched by few.
Can I sell paid lectures through YouTube unlisted links?

It is the wrong tool for paid lectures. Anyone with an unlisted link can watch and share it, so there is no real access control. Use YouTube for free lessons and host paid lectures behind a student login.
Vimeo, AWS or Bunny: which costs least for course videos?

All three are priced by plan tier or by GB delivered, so cost rises with views, and you still build the player, logins and access control. Hosting included in a teaching plan is usually simpler and keeps the cost known.
Does AllCoaching charge separately for storage or bandwidth?

Not inside your plan's allowance. Storage and streaming are included in every plan with no per-view bill. If you need more, you extend from the studio at ₹499 a month per extra 100 GB of storage or ₹399 per extra 100 GB of streaming.
What happens when my storage or streaming runs out?
Only uploaded video pauses until you extend from the studio or the next month starts. Your website, app, YouTube video and live classes keep running.
How many hours of lectures fit in my plan?

As an illustrative guide, 100 GB of storage holds about 50 hours of lectures, so Starter's 512 GB fits roughly 250 hours, Growth's 1 TB about 500 hours and Pro's 2 TB about 1,000 hours. Videos added from YouTube do not count.
Which AllCoaching plan has zero commission?
Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month) take 0% commission, so you keep 100% of every sale. Starter is ₹6,999 a year with a 10% fee on each sale. Prices exclude GST.
Do I need a CDN to host lectures for students across India?

Yes, in practice. A CDN keeps copies of your videos close to students so playback starts fast and buffers less on mobile networks. Hosting inside a teaching platform includes it; a file on a single server does not.
